findings.evidence: “not folded into a single vague sentence” repeats the immediately preceding requirement for two explicit numbered lists. The useful instruction is to derive both lists from the rendered TOML, not from the owner's earlier answers.
findings.fix: Keep the numbered-list example, the TOML read-back rule and the instruction to name missing keys. Consolidate the repeated presentation guidance into that rule and record the removal of the duplicate prose.

findings.evidence: “ask whether this local config should be `local-only` or the default `global-merge`” provides a default and storage syntax but no decision rule for an owner who expects the wizard's confirmed order to describe the effective roster.
findings.fix: At Step 2.8, ask whether this project should inherit any lanes or policy from the user roster. Keep `global-merge` when inheritance is wanted; explain that `local-only` is the choice when only the project roster should apply. Point to the layer rules in `references/config-file.md` when the owner wants details.

findings.evidence: The 1,012-character description is valid and gives clear boundaries, but “--check-only (report availability, no writes)” overpromises: the body says that live checks can affect runner state and the CLI can have its own side effects.
findings.fix: Use when the user wants to set up, refresh or check which AI models review plans or implement them, and in what fallback order, even without saying “lanes.” Detect installed CLIs and models, propose separate review and execute sets, and save the owner's choices, priority, effort and opt-ins in ai-kit's [lanes] table. Defaults to .aikit/config.toml; --local and --global choose a target, not permission to replace it. --check-only reports availability and stale opencode providers without saving ai-kit config, caches or trust; live probes can have side effects. Also use when ai-kit-spec-review or ai-kit-spec-execute-superpowers offers setup, or to explain review-spec.toml migration. Not for running configured lanes, hand-editing one lane, or editing [runner] or opencode.jsonc.

findings.evidence: The entry point is 442 lines and about 43 KB, with full subprocedures such as “Step 1.6 — Sort unknown skills (optional)” and role-confirm commands loaded even for check-only or headless runs. Its existing conditional references work well, but the core body still exceeds the recommended context budget.
findings.fix: Keep mode selection, write and migration gates, and the top-level workflow in SKILL.md. Move the complete optional role-sorting procedure and command examples to a new `references/skill-role-sorting.md`, linked directly at Step 1.6 and loaded only during interactive setup after the listing reports an addressable unsorted skill.

findings.evidence: “`SCRATCH="$(mktemp -d -t ai-kit-spec-config-XXXXXX)"; printf '%s\n' "$SCRATCH"`” prints even if creation fails; subsequent instructions construct write paths and a recursive cleanup command from that value.
findings.fix: Require successful creation of a nonempty absolute scratch path before printing or using it. If `mktemp` fails, report the error and stop before writing temporary files. Clean up only the confirmed directory created by this run, and apply the same guard to the check-only snippet.

findings.evidence: The stale-provider case says the live listing excludes `fake`, but supplies only the roster fixture, so the warning depends on the machine running the eval. The opencode-not-installed case likewise has no fixture for its CLI or config state. The check-only assertion “Keeps the run read-only” does not define what to compare.
findings.fix: Give the provider cases controlled CLI discovery and config fixtures: a successful listing that omits `fake` for the stale case, and an absent CLI with a synthetic opencode config for the fallback case. Assert the exact provider and certainty status. For check-only, compare config, cache and trust files before and after, and separately assert scratch cleanup.

findings.evidence: “Create a new SKILL.md for a changelog generator from scratch” is an easy negative in an otherwise useful near-miss set; it does not test the boundary between lane setup and other ai-kit configuration tasks.
findings.fix: Replace that query with a realistic near-miss, such as asking how to change the model catalog's source settings without configuring or checking any lanes.

findings.evidence: The wizard permits trust after a template-only preview. In the shared-key execute branch, the preview can omit the execute entry and step 7 can miss changes to its substitution fields. The trust command records the digest before the wizard compares the limited output.
findings.fix: Leave the roster untrusted when any command-bearing entry lacks a complete role-specific preview. To support that branch, make the preview cover both roles and have the trusting command require the approved digest, refusing before it writes a trust record if the digest has changed.

findings.evidence: “If `--check-only` was passed” has no equivalent for plain-language requests such as the shipped eval's “Just check which reviewers are available, and do not change anything.” Without the literal flag, the documented otherwise branch saves a runtimes snapshot.
findings.fix: Resolve mode from both flags and user intent before any persistent write. Route check-only requests to `references/check-only.md` without requiring the literal flag. If the user explicitly disallows all side effects, use detection and the provider report only, and mark live availability unknown.

findings.evidence: The no-fetch, no-catalog branch says “The first `confirm-catalog-entry` call creates `<catalog>`,” but the cross-reference supplies only the outer JSON envelope. The validator requires `provider`, `runtimes`, `source`, `confidence` and `last_verified`; a model ID alone is not enough to reach the proposal.
findings.fix: Add a validated minimal user-stated catalog-entry example next to the no-fetch procedure, including the canonical catalog key and runtime-to-model mapping. If the necessary fields cannot be established or the helper refuses the entry, use the documented session-default or stop path without fetching.

findings.evidence: “Pass `--catalog-path <catalog>` to `check-reviewer` so the result is recorded” overstates the command's contract. The custom-entry branch has no runtime and records nothing; a manually named pair absent from the catalog can return `usability.recorded: false` even after a live call.
findings.fix: Distinguish the live test result from catalog persistence. Report a catalog update only when `usability.recorded` is true; otherwise relay the reason if present. Say that custom entries are tested without a runtime-scoped catalog record.

findings.evidence: Step 4 presents the capability report as covering the saved roster. `config-status --cwd` reports the effective merged roster instead: after a global write, a project's `local-only` strategy can hide the newly saved lanes, and an ordinary merge can show inherited lanes.
findings.fix: Label the capability lines as the effective view for the named project and keep the saved-roster summary separate. If the write is global and the project is local-only, explain the shadowing rather than implying the preview covered the newly saved lanes.

findings.evidence: “codex has no `models`/`list-models` subcommand (confirmed via `codex --help`)” is a version-sensitive negative claim with no checked version or date. OpenAI's CLI source confirms the `debug models` route, but an undated past help check does not establish the installed binary's interface.
findings.fix: Drive the wizard from the live `detect-runtimes` result and use the installed binary's `codex debug --help` if troubleshooting a missing list. If retaining the negative claim as background, give the checked CLI version, date and official source.
